$schema: Instance config for an ai-bridge control panel. Customize, then commit. TRACKED, so every value here is a statement both clones of a shared bundle read; the per-machine half lives beside it in the gitignored instance.config.local.json, whose overridable set is listed in ONE place -- SCHEMA.md, 'Per-machine config overrides'. `models` and `roleTiers` below are SEEDED into that local file by install.sh and are kept here as the FALLBACK: with neither layer, scripts/resolve-model.sh resolves to nothing and every agent inherits the session model.
$people: EXAMPLE ONLY -- replace both entries below with your team's real GitHub login -> commit email pairs, HERE in this instance. The ai-bridge template is public, so it ships placeholder logins VERIFIED UNCLAIMED on github.com (example-user-007/008 both 404) and addresses at example.com, which RFC 2606 reserves and which cannot receive mail. If you write a new example, verify the login is unclaimed the same way: a plausible name like alice or bob is a real account, and an example naming a stranger is an example someone copies. The address is PER-INSTANCE, not per-person: the same login belongs to a different address in each group's bundle, because the address says which entity the work belongs to -- so never derive it from the login, and never move it into instance.config.local.json (that file says which login this clone IS). Used by scripts/commit-as.sh so each clone authors commits as the human running it; see SCHEMA.md 'Per-machine config overrides'. (install.sh offers to collect these when it stamps a NEW instance at a terminal; it never overwrites what is already here.)
$board: ON BY DEFAULT, and it is read at BOTH ends of the lifecycle. true (or absent) => install.sh creates SNAPSHOT.json when missing on any stamp, so this instance appears on the terminal board, AND each /ai-bridge:dispatch tick re-renders the page to .board-live/board.html (gitignored) and reports that path. false => the snapshot is never created, the installer says so, and the tick renders nothing and says nothing. NOTHING IS EVER PUBLISHED: the board is a LOCAL file on this machine, so this key costs no data-governance decision -- an instance whose board must not leave the machine can leave it on. (The account-scoped publish path, and the config key that recorded its URL, were deleted: only the publishing account could ever update the page, and it vanished from under its own owner at the next login.) Question TEXT still needs SNAPSHOT_QUESTION_TEXT=1 on top of this. scripts/watch-board.sh renders the same file continuously if you want it live between ticks.
$advisor: OPTIONAL read-only tick observer. Add "advisor" to roles to enable it, and set roleTiers.advisor to pick its model (absent => light, the cheapest tier). Omit it and /ai-bridge:dispatch skips that step silently. Its concerns are adjudicated by the deep-tier project-manager before any human sees them, and it has no channel to worker agents, so a cheap model can never steer an expensive one.
$roles: Agents the PM may dispatch as TASK ASSIGNEES. Not every configured agent belongs here — `plan-architect` is deliberately absent: `/plan` and the PM's approach critique dispatch it directly, and no task is ever assigned to it. See `$roleTiers` and SCHEMA.md 'type: Agent'.
$models: Which model alias each TIER costs. PER-MACHINE SPEND, and install.sh seeds this key into instance.config.local.json on any stamp that finds it missing there -- so on a stamped instance the LOCAL copy is the one in force and the session banner's FROM column reads `local`. This tracked copy stays as the fallback and as the seed source: removing it would let an unseeded instance resolve to nothing, and an agent that resolves to nothing inherits the session model with no error. Edit the LOCAL file to change what this machine pays; a partial local map overrides entry by entry, and the installer never tops it up. See SCHEMA.md, 'Per-machine config overrides'.
$roleTiers: PER-MACHINE SPEND, seeded and overridden exactly as `models` above (see `$models`). The model tier for ANY agent this instance dispatches, including ones no task is ever assigned to — broader than `roles`. `plan-architect: apex` here and nowhere in `roles` is the intentional case: `models.apex` today affects exactly that one agent, which appears in no `roles` list, so 'what does apex cost me?' is unanswerable from `roles` alone. Do not delete this row to make the two lists match; see SCHEMA.md 'type: Agent' and tests/roles-roletiers-asymmetry.test.sh.
